from.place: proof, affine sheaf-Hom adjunction and its counit

title: Affine restriction adjunction by derived internal Hom
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and write $A=f_*\mathcal O_Y$. On the derived categories of $A$-modules and $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-derived-category], restriction along $\mathcal O_X\to A$ has right adjoint $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_X}(A,-)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The counit at $K$ is the morphism $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_X}(A,K)\to K$ induced by evaluation at the unit section $1\in A$ (locally, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi(1)$).

source.place: Tag 0BV0, lemma-sheafhom-affine-adjoint, and Tag 0BUZ, lemma-compute-sheafhom-affine; Tag 0AX3, remark-trace-map-finite

proof.text: For the affine morphism $f:Y\to X$ with $A=f_*\mathcal O_Y$, the underived sheaf-Hom functor $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(A,-)$ from $\mathcal O_X$-modules to $A$-modules is right adjoint to restriction of scalars, and on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ with $f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ its sections are $\operatorname{Hom}_R(S,F(U))$ with counit evaluation at $1\in S$; this is the affine sheaf-Hom calculation of Tag 0AX2.

Apply the derived-adjunction theorem to the underived restriction/sheaf-Hom adjunction. Restriction of scalars is exact, so it preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces a functor $D(A)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$ which is an absolute left derived functor of itself; $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(A,-)$ is the right derived extension of $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(A,-)$, computed on K-injective resolutions, hence an absolute right derived functor. The theorem therefore gives an adjunction between restriction $D(A)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(A,-):D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(A)$.

source.place: Tag 0AX2, lemma-sheafhom-affine-adjoint, citing Derived Categories, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors

proof.text: The underived counit is evaluation at the unit: on an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ with $f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(S)$, the adjunction is restriction of scalars $S\text{-Mod}\to R\text{-Mod}$ and $R$-linear maps $S\to F(U)$, whose counit sends $\varphi$ to $\varphi(1)$. By the counit clause of [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived], the derived counit at a complex $K$ is compatible with the underived counit applied to $K$ (computed on a K-injective representative). Hence the component $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(A,K)\to K$ is induced by evaluation at $1\in A$.
